resources.string: Create your first scan to keep a clear, local record of your collection.
Read how PokeAndScan handles your data.
A local companion for making a clear, reviewable record of your Pokémon collection.

Your screen is processed on this device. You navigate Pokémon GO yourself. Anything uncertain stays available for your review. PokeAndScan is an unofficial companion app and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Pokémon GO or its creators.
Choose a capture source later, when you set up a scan. Capture and notification permissions are not needed for this introduction.
PokeAndScan reads the visible screen while you move through appraisal screens in Pokémon GO.
You can also select an Android screen recording and let PokeAndScan process it on this device.
PokeAndScan does not tap or swipe for you. You stay in control of Pokémon GO throughout the scan.
Use this short guide before your first scan. You can open it again from New scan at any time.

The verified reference is a Pixel 9 Pro XL running Android 10 or newer, in portrait orientation, with Pokémon GO in English and Android display size and font size set to their defaults. Other phones may install the app, but their scan support has not been verified.

Remove filters you did not mean to set. An intentional Pokémon GO filter or tag defines your scan scope, so keep it active if you want to scan only that selection. Sorting by Name A–Z can make a collection easier to traverse.
Nicknames are not supported as a scan field. A nickname can also hide a Pokémon’s species name, leaving the species for you to identify during review.

In Pokémon storage, open the first Pokémon and choose Appraise. Then use Pokémon GO’s on-screen arrows to move to the next Pokémon. Wait for each appraisal screen to settle before moving again. Keep moving through appraisal screens; returning to the storage list between every Pokémon is not the supported scan flow.
Pokémon GO is not installed on this device.
